description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage of different methods as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 0 to 65. The plot includes six lines representing different methods: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with square markers), and ROME (green line with cross markers). The Base method shows a relatively flat trend, maintaining an accuracy just above 45% across all co-occurrence numbers. MEND, FT, MEMIT, and IKE show a gradual increase in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with MEMIT and IKE reaching the highest accuracy, just below 60%. ROME shows the most significant increase, starting just above 50% and reaching approximately 65% at the highest co-occurrence number.
